issues.line_text: Five years of investigation. Two years of active surveillance. Almost a year of living a lie so complete I sometimes forgot it was a lie.
issues.description: Timeline contradiction. Lily died February 2020. Josh arrives October 2024. That's 4 years 8 months, not 5 years. Also, Eleanor's tenure at Thornewood is ~6 months (since April 2024), not 'almost a year.'
issues.fix: Two years of planning. Two years of active surveillance. Six months of living a lie so complete I sometimes forgot it was a lie.
issues.rationale: Aligns with Story Bible: Lily died Feb 2020, Eleanor investigated 2+ years after (2020-2022), lured Josh in 2024 after hearing his podcast announcement ~2 years prior. Eleanor claimed 6 months tenure at Thornewood (since ~April 2024).

issues.line_text: Lily's timeline. My timeline. Josh's timeline. All three converging on February 2020, right here at Thornewood.
issues.description: Timeline reference is correct for Lily's death (Feb 2020) and matches Story Bible.
issues.fix: NO FIX NEEDED - This line is accurate.
issues.rationale: This is actually correct upon review - Lily died Feb 2020 per Story Bible.

issues.line_text: I've spent two years building this case. I quit my job. Became a PI. Tracked every movement, every alias, every lie. I didn't come here on a hunch. I came here because I know.
issues.description: Eleanor says 'two years building this case' but the timeline shows Lily died Feb 2020 and Josh arrives Oct 2024 (4 years 8 months later). Eleanor's active investigation was 2+ years per Story Bible, but saying 'two years' in March 2025 is understating it.
issues.fix: I've spent years building this case. I quit my job. Became a PI. Tracked every movement, every alias, every lie. I didn't come here on a hunch. I came here because I know.
issues.rationale: Removes specific timeframe that creates math problems. 'Years' is vague enough to cover the 2+ years of investigation Eleanor conducted between 2020-2024.

issues.line_text: Six confirmed victims. Possibly more. The pattern goes back at least five years.
issues.description: Story Bible states pattern goes back to 2019 (Sarah Martinez, Oct 2019). Current date is March 2025. That's 5.5 years, which rounds to 'at least five years' - technically accurate but could be clearer as 'at least six years' since we're in early 2025.
issues.fix: Six confirmed victims. Possibly more. The pattern goes back to late 2019.
issues.rationale: More precise dating avoids rounding ambiguity. 'Late 2019' (Sarah Martinez, Oct 2019) to March 2025 is clearly the 5+ year span without math confusion.

issues.line_text: Tomorrow I have to reveal that every time we touched, every time we made love, every intimate moment between us was Eleanor sleeping with Lily's killer.
issues.description: This internal thought is fine for Eleanor's POV, but the phrase 'sleeping with Lily's killer' is very direct. Eleanor would know this more viscerally - it's not an abstraction to her.
issues.fix: Tomorrow I have to reveal that every time we touched, every time we made love, every intimate moment between us was me betraying my sister with the man who strangled her.
issues.rationale: More visceral and personal. Eleanor's guilt is about betraying Lily specifically, not the abstract concept of 'the killer.' Makes the emotional truth sharper without changing spoiler level.

notes: Chapter is remarkably clean overall. The main issues are timeline math (5 years vs. 4.8 years since Lily's death, 'almost a year' at Thornewood vs. 6 months established). The emotional core and reveals are well-executed. Eleanor's voice maintains appropriate investigator tone while revealing her grief. The letter is a strong narrative device. The footage scene is visceral without being gratuitous. One minor issue: Eleanor says she's watched the footage '237 times' - hyper-specific number feels authentic to obsessive reviewing. No spoiler leaks detected about protected twists (Josh's mother, Eleanor's identity already revealed at this point in story).
